subject: Embeddings cutover: SDK auth, routing & reranker tuning
messages:
From: Sara Liu <sara.liu@retaily.com>
To: karthik_iyer@example.com, marissa_cole@example.com, ben_carter@example.com
Cc: Aleks Novak <aleks@retaily.com>
Date: 2026-11-30T16:12:00-05:00
Subject: Follow-up: embedding migration needs and architecture questions

Thanks again for the call earlier today — quick recap and a few asks so we can get an internal alignment at Retailly. High-level goals: move off our incumbent embeddings provider, consolidate vector store, reduce tail latency, and enable a reranker for search relevance.

Key constraints we mentioned:
- Existing embeddings: 1024-dimension float32 vectors, ~300M vectors, daily 200k new vectors.
- Peak QPS for lookups: roughly 550 RPS with median batch size ~8.
- Security: data-in-transit & at-rest controls; SOC2 evidence required for procurement.

Primary questions / asks for Redwood:
1) SDK & auth: what are the recommended auth flows for server-to-server ingestion jobs (long-running reindex)? API keys, service accounts, short-lived tokens?
2) Dimensions & mapping: recommendations for target vector dimension — we may re-embed (costly) vs. mapping strategy to keep legacy vectors usable.
3) Batching & normalization: recommended batch sizes for re-embed jobs and whether L2-normalization is preferred vs. unitizing at query time.
4) Reranker integration: expectations for candidate set size, calling pattern (sync vs async), and any structured output/tool calling you recommend for score provenance.

Next steps we want from Redwood this week:
- Mutual action plan / cutover checklist (who does what, timeline, test signal).
- A short SDK snippet showing ingestion + auth best practice.
- Any migration utilities (partial re-embed pipeline, mapping helpers).

Happy to share a small sample (10k rows) of our vectors and the schema. Can we schedule a 60-min technical working session next Tue or Wed?

Thanks,
Sara
VP Search & Recommendations
Retailly

From: karthik_iyer@example.com

Subject: Re: Follow-up: embedding migration needs and architecture questions

Sara — thanks for the clear recap. Appreciate the constraints; below are pragmatic answers and what we'll bring to the technical session. I attached a one-page cutover checklist (redwood-embed-cutover-checklist.xlsx) and a tiny auth patches file with examples for service-account flows.

Quick answers (TL;DR):
- SDK & auth: For long-running server-to-server jobs we recommend using short-lived service account tokens (OAuth 2.0 JWT flow) with a scoped "embeddings:write" role. API keys are OK for small, ad-hoc jobs but less audit-friendly. We'll provide a short-lived token rotation example in the SDK.

- Dimensions & mapping: If you plan to re-embed, we suggest moving to 1536 dims (modern open models) for quality/cost balance. For a mapping approach (avoid full re-embed), we can provide a mapping layer that learns a linear projection from your 1024 -> 1536 space using ~100k paired samples. It's a reasonable interim to get parity for reranker inputs while you re-embed gradually.

- Batching & normalization: For bulk re-ingest, start with batch sizes of 256 for CPU pre-processing and 64 concurrent async workers for the upload phase (we'll throttle to avoid IO spikes). For runtime inference, dynamic batching targeting 32-128 depending on latency SLO is typical. We strongly recommend L2-normalizing vectors at index time and keeping queries normalized to avoid mismatched norms.

- Reranker integration: Typical pattern we recommend — candidate generation (approx NN) -> lightweight scorer (embedding dot-prod) -> neural reranker for top N (N=50 by default). Neural reranker should be called synchronously if you need sub-200ms end-to-end; otherwise async for background personalization. We'll demo structured output for the reranker (score + provenance) so you can show why an item ranked higher.

What we'll bring to the tech session:
- A proposed M.A.P. (mutual action plan) with phased cutover and rollback windows.
- SDK quickstart snippets for ingestion, service-account token rotation, and a routing policy snippet that handles fallback between models during capacity issues.
- A small mapping toolkit (linear projection trainer) and guidance for when to do full re-embed.

Proposed times: Tue Dec 1 10:00-11:00 AM ET or Wed Dec 2 9:00-10:00 AM ET — which works?

Thanks — I'll loop Ben to give a concrete SDK snippet and Marissa on commercial items.

— Karthik Iyer
Sr. Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Sara — quick engineering follow-up and a small SDK snippet below. Also attaching an auth example patch (auth-snippets.patch).

SDK ingestion + auth (pseudo-JS):
```
const Redwood = require('@redwood/inference-sdk');
const client = new Redwood.Client({auth: {type: 'service_account', tokenUrl: 'https://auth.redwood.example/token'}});
// bulk ingest helper handles batching and retry
await client.embeddings.bulkIngest({
  datasetUri: 's3://retaily-samples/10k.csv',
  batchSize: 256,
  normalize: 'l2'
});
```

Routing policy (high level):
- route by tenant: retailly-prod -> high-throughput pool (quantized variants)
- fallback: if primary model saturated, route to cheaper 1536-quantized variant with lower token precision

Reranker notes:
- Candidate set: start N=100, rerank top 50 for production tuning.
- For provenance, include structured output: {score, model_version, reason_tokens}. We'll show a sample structured response in the tech session.

Security note: we support both API key & OAuth; for long-running jobs prefer rotating service account tokens. Attached patch includes an example rotation script and minimal IAM roles.

Attachment: auth-snippets.patch (patch, 2KB)

Looking forward to the session — I'll prepare the projection trainer and a short demo mapping 1024->1536 with a small dataset.

— Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
